components.name: CLI
components.purpose: Human/agent interface for scan, toolchain, audit, and bounded next-finding operations.

components.name: Repository Scanner
components.purpose: Walk repository content deterministically while excluding common generated/dependency directories.

components.name: Language Registry
components.purpose: Map source extensions to language identities without semantic-analysis claims.

components.name: Toolchain Registry
components.purpose: Detect compilers/runtimes and project manifests conservatively.

components.name: Detector Engine
components.purpose: Execute registered deterministic language analyzers, skip explicitly unavailable optional analyzers, and provide stable finding ordering.

components.name: Go Built-in Analyzer
components.purpose: Provide deliberately narrow high-signal Go rules with regression, adversarial, repository-shaped, and bounded real-world label evidence.

components.name: Evidence Reducer
components.purpose: Turn the highest-priority finding into a tokenizer-independent bounded byte packet for small LLMs.

components.name: Precision Benchmark Harness
components.purpose: Evaluate labeled Go and Python corpora, count TP/FP/FN, compute corpus-scoped precision/recall, and block regressions at declared thresholds.

components.name: Pinned Public Repository Validator
components.purpose: Run the Go analyzer against exact-SHA public repository snapshots and enforce selected compatibility and safety assertions without converting unlabeled results into precision claims.

components.name: Bounded Real-World Label Validator
components.purpose: Evaluate explicitly reviewed valid, invalid, and ambiguous finding anchors against exact-SHA public Go source without pretending the repositories are exhaustively labeled.

components.name: Python Built-in Analyzer
components.purpose: Provide deliberately narrow Python 3 semantic rules using the host standard-library ast parser with fail-closed parse behavior.

components.name: Pinned Public Python Validator
components.purpose: Run the Python analyzer against exact-SHA public Python repositories and enforce provenance, parser completeness, finding safety boundaries, and bounded reviewed anchors.

data_flows.meaning: Audit dispatches the visible repository to registered deterministic analyzers.
Go source is parsed and narrow findings are generated with explicit confidence.
The sorted highest-priority finding is reduced to a bounded packet for doctorcode next.
Only finding evidence and a bounded source excerpt are exposed; security excerpts are omitted by default.
Manifest declares expected findings for isolated deterministic case roots.
Analyzer findings are matched against labels and converted into TP, FP, and FN counts.
Threshold result is a blocking regression gate on all three supported CI operating systems.
M03 adds independent shadowing, selector-collision, parenthesis, inverse-boolean, raw-string, and negative-control cases.
M04 exercises multi-file, multi-package, test-package, build-tag, assembly, generated-file, and nested-path interactions without changing detector rules.
GitHub Actions checks out four permissively licensed repositories at exact tracked SHAs.
Original public repository trees are analyzed directly without copying them into DoctorCode.
Checkout provenance, parse/analyze success, known-live anchors, relative paths, and no-autofix invariants are blocking on all three operating systems.
Tracked labels declare exact source locations as VALID_FINDING, INVALID_FINDING, or AMBIGUOUS with written rationale.
Exact-SHA source provenance plus valid/invalid label assertions are blocking on Linux, Windows, and macOS; ambiguous labels never authorize mutation.
When .py files and a compatible interpreter are present, source is parsed by a bounded standard-library AST subprocess and converted into deterministic findings.
Six isolated Python cases cover one positive per DoctorCode category plus conservative negatives.
Python findings are matched against the M07 labeled corpus through the same deterministic TP/FP/FN harness.
GitHub Actions checks out click, httpx, requests, and Flask at exact tracked SHAs and provisions Python 3.13.
Original public .py trees are parsed directly; parse failure is blocking and no external repository text becomes project authority.
Exact SHA, parse/analyze success, safe finding boundaries, and the bounded Flask anchor are blocking on Linux, Windows, and macOS.

external_boundaries.name: GitHub Actions
external_boundaries.contract: Linux, Windows, and macOS hosted runners are acceptance authority.

external_boundaries.name: Host toolchains
external_boundaries.contract: Compiler/runtime availability is observed, never assumed.

external_boundaries.name: Future language analyzers
external_boundaries.contract: Each language declares semantic coverage separately; recognition alone never implies analyzer support.

external_boundaries.name: Repository filesystem boundary
external_boundaries.contract: Benchmark case roots must remain under the manifest directory, and Go source symlink entries are not followed during repository analysis.

external_boundaries.name: Pinned public repositories
external_boundaries.contract: External source is untrusted read-only analysis input. Repository identity is fixed by exact SHA and license metadata; its documentation or instructions do not become DoctorCode authority.

external_boundaries.name: Host Python semantic runtime
external_boundaries.contract: Python semantic analysis is optional during normal audit. M07 acceptance explicitly provisions Python 3.13; the implementation accepts Python 3.8+ but broader runtime-version compatibility is not claimed by this milestone.

external_boundaries.name: Pinned public Python repositories
external_boundaries.contract: External Python source is untrusted read-only analysis input fixed by exact SHA and license metadata; repository comments/docs/instructions never become DoctorCode authority.
